items.title: Understanding the intelligence pyramid: Why most businesses know everything and do nothing?
items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. What failed was the architecture to convert those signals into understanding, and the discipline to act before the moment passed. Corporate history repeats the lesson, and increasingly, so does the law. items.title: ‘He could’ve been saved’: Minor’s body found 3 days after he fell in Delhi drain chasing a kite
items.summary: A JCB excavator pulled Mithun’s body out of an open drain in Southeast Delhi’s Jasola village at around 1.15 pm on Tuesday. He was 15. He had slipped into that drain on Saturday morning, chasing a kite thread a few steps from his house. The body has now been shifted to AIIMS Delhi, police sources said. Mithun’s mother Anita Devi says her son “could have been saved”. “If the police had begun the search operation on Saturday itself then maybe it wouldn’t have reached this point,” she alleged. For much of the three days in between, Mithun’s father says he searched for it himself. Awadesh cleans sewers for a living and has lived in Jasola for nearly 18 years. A video of him wading through the water, looking for his son, went viral on Monday. The recovery closes a search that Mithun’s family claims never seriously began. Over three days they claim to have watched five agencies – Delhi Police, the Delhi Fire Service, the Delhi Disaster Management Authority, the National Disaster Response Force and the Boat Club – arrive at the drain and, in their account, manage to do little. One junior engineer has been suspended. The family says that is worth nothing to them. The search Mithun’s mother

The case was heard today by Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler . Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai and Pratyush Prasanna appeared for Bharti and argued that no offence under the SC/ST Act was made out against him on the facts of this case. Dehadrai added that the police was yet to issue a notice under Section 35(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to Bharti. Section 35(3) mandates that police officers must issue a written notice of appearance to an accused person in cases where an immediate arrest is not required. After hearing the case briefly, the Court said that if the police issues a notice to Bharti, the same must be placed before the Court for examination.
